en: He whose elder brother is the illustrious Sanātana, who is equal to Sanātana himself; he who is the beloved of Śrī, the younger brother of Anuja, that Śrīrūpa, the true refuge of the individual soul. ||1||

The Lord, the son of Śrī and Śacī, the Sovereign who is intent upon those various states of being, has descended as Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age for the sake of all those who have taken refuge in Him and are devoted to Him. 2.

The wise indeed worship Him who is black in color yet blackless in splendor, together with His limbs, secondary limbs, weapons, and attendants, primarily through sacrifices consisting of congregational chanting. ||3||
The one God, Kṛṣṇacandra, the most exalted, whose nature is eternal bliss— may that Lord divide Himself into two, like Gaṅgārī, for our sake. 4.
The second is indeed the Self who delights in non-duality and so forth;
he possesses many principal powers, such as the glorious Rūpā;
the Lord bestows shade upon those scorched by the heat [of worldly existence]. ||5||
That salutation and that remembrance bestow all spiritual accomplishments;
by what living being could they be performed who does not know their proper sequence? (6)
O great ones whose minds are fixed on Kṛṣṇa, please forgive my offenses. Just as you truly know each other here, so may the Blessed Lord speak, acting according to your instructions. (8)
I bow to Śacī and Jagannātha, who are the very embodiments of Yaśodā and Nanda, whose two sons are the gods Viśvarūpa and Viśvambhara. (9)
Now I pay homage to that wondrous Caitanyāgra, known as Śaṅkarāraṇya, the king of the assembly of renunciants and the universal form. 10.
I bow to Śrī Gauracandra, whose body is composed of aesthetic rasa, who assumes the state of Śrī Rādhikā’s Śrī Hari in order to experience here the essence of that mass of splendor and compassion,
and who seeks to uplift the multitudes of living beings defiled by the impurities of the Kali age and devoid of all devotion.
He who was born in the midst of Śrī Navadvīpa, surrounded by a multitude of attendants, is indeed one whose sleep is blissful. 11.
For he who is indeed the second body of the Lord is the god Gadādhara. ||12||
And he was a disciple of that treasury of knowledge, a mine of the sentiment of devotion to his master;
he was that steadfast Gadādhara, beloved by all devotees. (13)
I bow to Padmāvatī and her husband, the scholar Haḍḍipa;
I bow to Nityānandadeva, the self-effulgent Lord Balabhadra, the root of bliss, the fearless one, the Guru who delivers the world. (15)
That very Puruṣa, who is Prakṛti itself, through the distinction between external and internal, performs the service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa by means of various bodily forms. 16.
I bow to the illustrious Queen Vasudhā, the beloved of Lord Nityānanda, the daughter of Śrī Sūryadāsa, who was awakened by the power of the Supreme Lord. (17)
I pay homage to the goddess Śrījāhnavī, the disciple of the Lord of Śrīpura, whom those who know the secret call by the name Anaṅgamañjarī. (18)
At his command, as the Lord was departing after casting off that physical form, she of firm vows served him with supreme love, [seeking] eternal bliss. ||19||
Constantly drawn by the pangs of separation, the Mistress who dwells in the Vṛndā forest, desiring to see the Lord of the Gopīs, pulled at His waist-knot. 20.
The goddess Ākṛṣṭanīvikā said to him, who was filled with the rising of aesthetic delight:
"I shall quickly come to the place near your feet. (21)
I bow to Lord Vīracandra, the Hari who is Śrī Caitanya Prabhu, who has manifested as a second incarnation and is the savior of the three worlds. (22)

There, one devoted to the Vedic dharma, free from worldly attachment, devoid of ego, and without deceit—though appearing to possess the semblance of pride—is indeed a servant of the Ganges in this world. (23)
[She who is] the daughter of Lord Nityānanda, whose essence is the union of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, the wife of Mādhavācārya, and whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss. (24)
I bow to the most excellent Gaṅgā, the mother of the worlds, headed by Śrī Premamañjarī; she is the bestower of love and the purifier of the three realms. 25.
That Gaṅgā, the disciple of Jāhnavī, purifies the three worlds—even with the lords who are themselves purifying—having her flow stolen by Viriñca until the end of the aeon. ||26||

The ornament of the twice-born family, who has descended [to earth], who has entered the Gaṅgā desiring to take her up, Mādhava, whose form is that of Mādhava, whose body consists of aesthetic rasa, and who is known as Love (Premākhyam). ||27||
And he was the disciple of Īśvarapurī, a purifier of all philosophical systems, preeminent among the devotees of Viṣṇu, and adorned with a multitude of excellent virtues. (28)
Having deliberated upon these, the wise one, who is a treasure-house of compassion, set aside ritual action and knowledge and determined the true nature of love for Kṛṣṇa. (29)
I bow to Mādhavendra, the ornament of the Yati lineage, the ancient lord of sages, and the devotee of the primordial Lord Īśvara; he who made manifest devotion to Hari. (30)
I bow to the non-dual, compassionate, and supremely merciful Śāmbhava abode, by whom,
through his austerities, the son of Śacī was brought here along with his retinue,
as well as Sītā— the beloved of that Lord, the mother of the three worlds, who is the power (Śakti) of Kailāsa and other realms.
But for her, Śrī Jagannātha was pleased and bestowed his grace throughout the three worlds. //31//
I bow to that Supreme Bliss, the beloved of Kṛṣṇacaitanya,
who is known as Acyuta and is the knower of the true nature of Śrī Kṛṣṇacaitanya;
for others, many of whom were destroyed by fate, did not indeed respect him.
O Acyuta, those who have died by your will should be abandoned and disregarded as being afflicted by disease.
I bow to Śrīvāsa Nārada, the mother of Mālinī, and then to the goddess Nārāyaṇī, who partakes of the nectar of the lower lip. ||34||
[He who] describes the qualities of the glorious Nityānanda Caitanya. ||35||
I bow to Haridāsa, the abode of Brahman, who reveals the name of Hari; I salute Paṇḍita Jagadānanda, who is the very embodiment of the Goddess of Speech. (36)
I then bow to Gopīnātha, the author of the hymn to Caitanya;
I bow to Śrī Candraśekhara, who is ever as cooling as the moon;
and to Govinda Garuḍa, the jewel among teachers, whose mind is as fair as gold. (38)
I bow to the noble-minded Mukundadatta, who is intoxicated by singing the songs of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s stainless virtues and who is being praised by the Kinnaras. (39)
I bow to Vāsudevadatta, who is filled with great qualities;
by the touch of the wind from his body, one immediately becomes possessed of the pair of divine loves (prema). (40)
I bow to Dāmodara and Pītāmbara, and to Jagannātha, Śaṅkara, and Nārāyaṇa; I salute those five noble-minded holy men who are free from worldly desires. 41.
I pay homage to the sovereign Nīlāmbara-cakravartin, renowned as Prabhumātāma, who composed the Koṣṭhī, which is endowed with descriptions of the future. (42)
I salute Śrī Rāmapaṇḍita, who is devoted to the welfare of all beings, and the noble-minded Śrī Gupta Nārāyaṇa, the sole abode of virtues. (43)
I salute my supreme guru Gaṅgādāsa, who made his residence at Navadvīpa, as well as Śrī Viṣṇudāsa, known by the name Śrī Sudarśana. 44.
I ever revere Sadāśiva, the treasury of knowledge, and Śrīgarbha;
as well as Śrīnidhi, the wise one, and the supreme Śrīlaśuklāmbara. 45.
O celibate student, these indeed are my dear ones:
the magnanimous ones, as well as Śrī Rāmadāsa and Kavicandra, the treasure-house of compassion. ||46||
Śrīdhara, Udāra, the renowned [one], and Vanamālin together with his sons. 47.
I bow to Halāyudha and Vāsudeva, who are the very essence of Śrī Caitanya’s mind and are pure;
and I bow to Īśānadāsa, the recipient of Śacīdevī’s affection. (48)
I reverently salute the illustrious Sañjaya and his son, who are full of compassion, who possess the marks of supreme bliss, and whose minds are absorbed in pure consciousness. 49.
I bow to Garuḍa, Kāśīśvara, Jagadīśa, Gaṅgādāsa, both of them, as well as the sweet Kṛṣṇānanda and the supreme Rāyamukunda. 50.
I pay homage to the venerable teacher Vallabha, who delighted the daughter of Lakṣmī and bestowed her upon Śacī’s husband, that bridegroom who is a mass of virtues. (51)
Furthermore, I salute the eternal Paṇḍita, who is endowed with virtues, by whom Viṣṇupriyā was given in marriage to Śacījā. (52)
I bow to the brahmin Kāśīnātha, the preceptor Vanamālī, who devised the plan for the sake of Lakṣmīdevī’s marriage. (53)
I bow to Śrī Keśavabhāratī, whom the Lord Caitanya, having taken as his guru, honored himself by the name Dhanya. (54)
I bow to Śrī Keśavabhāratī, who is honored by the assembly of renunciants; by her, the great lord [Caitanya] was made a renunciant who had laid down his worldly duties. ||55||
Then I salute the city of Rāmacandra, which is always under the control of its Lord;
it is the supreme bliss of the holy city, whose innocent interpretation is dear to Hari. (56)
Thereafter, I salute Dāmodarapurī, which is equal to Satyabhāmā;
thereafter, I salute Narasiṃhatīrtha, the city of happiness and bliss. (57)
Then [he saw] Govindānanda by name, Brahmānandapurī, Nṛsiṃhānanda by name, Satyānanda, and Bhāratī. ||58||
I bow to Garuḍāvadhauta, who is endowed with wonderful love;
thereafter, I bow to Viṣṇupurī, the author of the Bhaktiratnāvalī. 59.
Then, with supreme devotion and joy, I bow to the city of Kṛṣṇānanda, whose nature is the bliss of Brahman, and to the city of Śrī Rāghava. 60.
I bow to Viśveśvarānanda, and after him to Śrī Keśavapurī; I then bow to Anubhavānanda, to Citānanda, and to Sucittaka. (61)
I bow to those two lords, Rūpa and Sanātana, who are supreme bliss, detached, compassionate, and residents of Vṛndāvana. (62)
May I, even while bearing the slightest trace of the scent of impurity upon my feet, serve those two lotus-feet in birth after birth in this very world. (63)
The illustrious Śrīrūpa, endowed with lordly power and a treasure-house of mercy, having deliberated upon all the scriptures, determined the ultimate reality to be supreme love for Kṛṣṇa. (64)
The eternal Sanātana, free from all worldly expectations, performed the service of his devotee Gopālabhaṭṭa by composing works such as the *Haribhaktivilāsa*. (65)
That wise Gopālabhaṭṭa, remaining in the presence of Sanātana and delighting in the virtues of Hari, spent his days and nights here in happiness. (66)
Having heard that description of the qualities of the Lord's form as uttered by him, Gopālabhaṭṭa indeed constantly regarded himself as truly blessed, for he [perceived] Him on all sides. ||67||
I bow to Raghunāthadāsa, a resident of Rādhākuṇḍa, who knows the entire truth of Caitanya and has abandoned all other supreme states of being. 68.
I bow with a special devotion to the Gosvāmin named Rāghava, the noble-minded one who sports on Govardhana and wanders about. (69)
I reverently salute Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, the teacher of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, as well as Lokanātha Gosvāmī and the pure Bhūgarbha Ṭhakkura. (70)
I revere the stainless Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī, by whom, with joy, the *Candrāmṛta* was composed, and whose disciple is Gopālabhaṭṭa. (71)
Then I salute the Lord of Kāśī, then Śuddhasarasvatī, and then Rāghavānanda, who experiences eternal bliss. (72)
In whose house the illustrious son of Padmāvatī, full of curiosity, once fastened a *nīpa* flower upon a pomegranate tree. (73)
I salute Purandara here together with Aṅgada, since a certain excellent brahmin beheld his tail within the house. (74)
I bow to the most excellent Kāśī Miśra, who resides in Utkala and is perfectly pure; in whose hermitage the fair-complexioned Hari dwelt, worshipped by his devotion. (75)
Then I salute Vāṇīnātha, whose life is the glorious Jagannātha;
then I salute Rāmānanda, who is filled with the characteristics of devotion. 76.
From whose mouth, like from a cloud, the compassionate one has rained down upon the earth the nectar of the collection of principles for the perfection of his own devotion through consciousness. (77)
Then I bow to Vakreśvara, the heart of the Lord, which is so difficult to attain;
it is for the sake of the bliss of love for him that the Lord performed the kīrtana. (78)
I pay homage to that excellent brahmin Govinda, known as Sugrīvamīśra, whose greatness through the yoga of devotion is well-known throughout the earth. (79)
Indeed, for the sake of the Lord’s journey from the land of Śrī Navadvīpa to the Gauḍa country, he has built a mental bridge by which [the path] is secured. (80)
I bow here to Gadādhara, the servant of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, whose body is non-different from Śrī Kṛṣṇa and who is the very embodiment of Mahābhāva. ॥81॥
I salute Sadāśiva, the Physician, by whose touch even a stone indeed immediately attains fluidity; how much more so, then, other sentient beings? ||82||
I bow to Śivānandāsena, who is devoted to steadfastness and peace, he who knows nothing other than the feet of the Lord. 83.
I bow to that Mukundadāsa, whose son was Raghunandana, who, like Kāma the lord of Rati, caused Gopāla to eat a sweetmeat ball (laḍḍu). 84.
Even today, the devotion of Śrī Mukundadāsa is sung by people;
he who, upon seeing a peacock's tail, was drawn away by love for Kṛṣṇa. (85)
Immediately overcome with agitation, yet blissful with supreme joy, and no longer perceiving external functions, he fell down from his great position. 86.
I worship with devotion Narahari Dāsa, who is the manifestation of the sentiment offered to Caitanya;
he is the meritorious and blessed one named Madhumatī, who perceives no one other than Kṛṣṇa. (87)
And he is this most excellent delight of the Raghus, the disciple of Narahari, who is virtuous and whose character has been pure from childhood, his heart purified by devotion. (88)
I now salute Dāsa, known as Raghunātha,
whose conduct is noble; Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa, who places his hope in the feet of Hari, and Purandara Ācārya.
He is peaceful, compassionate, and beloved by the Blessed One and the people. ||89||
I bow to Prabhū Satīrtha, indeed to Paramānanda Paṇḍita,
and to Devānanda Paṇḍita, the reciter of the Śrīmad Bhāgavata;
I bow to the jewel among teachers (Ācārya Ratna), who has realized the core of the essence of divine love.
Govinda, Mādhava, Ānanda, Vāsudeva, and Guṇākara—[these were the names of the sons]. 91.
I bow to the servant named Puruṣottama, who is endowed with sovereign power;
he who transformed the karavīra flower into one possessing the fragrance of a lotus. 92.
I bow to the most delightful servant who is indeed Śrīdāmā himself on this earth;
I bow to Śrī Sundarānanda, who takes the form of the cowherd Sudāmā, whose disciple here bestows the name of Hari upon the multitude of the twice-born. (94)
I bow to Śrī Gaurīdāsa, Gopāla, and the one named Subala, by whom the Lord of Non-duality (Advaita Ṭhakkura) was led to supreme bliss in Mutphala. 95.
By the mere sight of whose form, the bondage of karma is instantly destroyed. (96)
Therefore, I salute the Supreme Lord, the illustrious master who is self-luminous, who, while dancing, caused even jackals to hear the name of Hari. (97)
Then I bow to Pippilāyi, who was overwhelmed by his state of childhood;
I bow to Kamalākaradāsa, whose bliss consists in the congregational chanting of the Lord's names. 98.
I bow to the holy site named Puruṣottama, the crest-jewel of connoisseurs;
and then I bow with love to Kāliyākṛṣṇadāsa, who is overwhelmed by that very same love. 99.
I bow to Śāraṅgaṭhakkura, whose majesty is self-manifested, by whom his own dwellings were granted as abodes to the serpents. (100)
Then I salute Makaradhvaja, who is beautiful as the sole abode of virtues, he who always performs the chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s glories in the presence of the Lord. (101)
Then [he met] the Bhāgavata teacher Śrī Kavirāja Miśra, as well as the teacher Ananta residing in Navadvīpa. ||102||
I bow to the scholar named Govindācārya, who is called Madhva, and who thereafter described the secret of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. (103)
Then I salute Bṛhaspati Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, and then Pratāparudra, by whom the six-armed Lord was beheld. (104)
I bow to the Brahmin Raghunātha, the physician Śrī Viṣṇudāsa;
I bow to his brother Dāsa, who wears a garland of forest flowers. ||105||
Then there was the twice-born Haridāsa, residing in Utkala with Vipradāsa, by whom Hari, the son of Śacī, was brought under their control through love. (106)
I bow to Kānāī Khūṭṭiyā, the mine of the nectar of love for Kṛṣṇa, whose two auspicious sons are both Jagannātha and Balarāma. (107)
I bow with devotion to the Lord of the World, Govinda, who is named Ānanda, and to the noble Ṭhakkura, by whose singing the trees here weep as if helpless;
I bow to him by whom, for the sake of the Lord, the mental bridge has been constructed. (109)
Then I salute the Lord of Kāśī, known by the name Śrī Siṃheśvara;
with supreme devotion, I salute Mādhava, the leader of Paṭṭana. 110.
Then I salute Haribhaṭṭa, and thereafter Mahātiṅga Baladeva;
then Subuddhimiśra, and thereafter the most excellent Śrīnāthamiśra. 111.
I bow to the venerable Śrītulasīmiśra, the great ascetic Kāśīnātha, and Rāmānanda, the foremost of the Vasu lineage, together with his circle of disciples. 112.
Both the scholar named Madhva, a celibate student of Puruṣottama, and the other were servants of the Lord Śrī Caitanya; they were compassionate and noble-minded. (113)
These [sages] are possessed of great compassion and are indifferent toward all worldly things;
I bow to the twice-born Rāmacandra, the scholar Śrīdhara, who has bestowed wealth. 114.
His dispassion was well-known; having surrendered all his possessions to the Lord, that high-souled scholar took up only a staff and a loincloth. (115)
Then I salute the learned Śrī Jagannātha Ācārya, then Lakṣaṇa, then Kṛṣṇadāsa, and the scholar Sūryadāsa. (116)
Then I worship Kṛṣṇavaṃśī, the noble master whose face is the flute, the servant of Murāri and Caitanya, who sports like a serpent. 117.
I pay homage to Jagannāthasena, to Paramānandagupta, to Bālaka known as Rāmadāsa, and thereafter to Kavicandra. 118.
I bow to Śrī Vallabhācārya, and then to Kaṃsārisena;
I also bow to Bhāskara, who is the very embodiment of Viśvakarman. (119)
I bow to Balarāmadāsa, who is characterized as a teacher of the Gītā, for he serves the Supreme Bliss and indeed possesses the splendor of Nityācārya. 120.
I bow to Paṇḍita Maheśa, who is overwhelmed by the intoxication of Kṛṣṇa;
I bow to the dancing Paṇḍita, the scholar known as Jagadīśa. ||121||
He [protected] the nobleman Kṛṣṇadāsa, who was devoted to Nityānanda, for he indeed worshipped the deity Nityānanda in his own home with devotion. (122)
By whom can the greatness of Gaurīdāsa’s beloved be described—he who, due to separation from eternal bliss, became distraught for seven months? (123)
Having granted me a further vision, he made me perfectly steadfast; I now bow to that most excellent Avadhūta, known as Paramānanda. 124.
I salute the scholar Vilāsin, known as Dāsa Śrī Yadunātha, who is free from beginningless bondage and possesses a sweet heart. 125.
I bow to the holy site of Śrī Puruṣottama and to Jagannātha known as Rāma;
I bow to the holy site of Vāsudeva and then to the glorious Ānandapurī. 126.
I bow to Mukundakavirāja, then to Rājīvapaṇḍita, and to Śrījīvapaṇḍita, who is endowed with every excellent quality. (127)
I bow to that auspicious and pure body which is sacred, full of bliss, and whose devotion to the feet of Śrī Caitanyacandra is perfectly stainless. 128.
I bow to him who bestowed salvation, who is ever united with eternal bliss, who wandered to all sacred fords, and whose soul was pure and free from worldly expectations. (129)
I worship the venerable Mādhavācārya, the bringer of auspiciousness to Kṛṣṇa;
and after him, Nṛsiṃha Caitanya’s servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa. (130)
I pay homage to the auspicious Ghoṣa, the supreme among those possessing nothing, who held the conch in his hand; that deity who, through the sound of his conch, gratified the son of Śacī. 131.
Again and again I bow to that Vaiṣṇava, the sovereign Śivānanda, who bears the name of Śrī Nārāyaṇa. ||132||
One should offer salutation to each of them individually and likewise pronounce their names—those who are radiant with special qualities and endowed with the virtue of non-attachment. (133)
For those high-souled Vaiṣṇavas who do not know the ultimate reality, this is the incomparable and supreme cause of their stainless purity, [the dust] from the feet of the Lord. (134)

The first devotee was named Mādhavendra Pūrī, who was likewise a guru; his qualities were such that the servants of Kṛṣṇacaitanya became like forest fires for the destruction of worldly attachment. ||135||
Some [attained it] through the gateway of Advaita, others through the gateway of Sītā; likewise, some through the gateway of Padmāvatī’s son and others through the gateway of the Jāhnavī. ||136||
Some [entered] through the gate of Gadādhara, and likewise some through the gate of Śrīrūpa;
some through the gate of Sanātana, and some through Haridāsa. ||137||
Some [were composed] by Raghunāthadāsa, some by Vakreśvara, some by Kāśīśvara, and likewise by Narahari as well. (138)
By Raghunandana, some here [were blessed], by the sovereign [Raghunātha], others;
likewise, other devotees were favored by one, and the servants of those [devotees] here by yet others. (139)
Therefore, he has gone for refuge to Śrī Kṛṣṇacaitanya himself—the worshipful Lord of the universe and the Teacher of the World—who is manifestly composed of all those various forms. (140)
Those devotees who have been brought down here by Kṛṣṇa as his eternal companions, and those who have been honored and praised for specific purposes; ||141||

The servants (dāsa), the powers (śakti), and likewise those who are of the nature of the portions (aṃśa)—the distinction between these is to be understood from the nectar of the Śrīmad Bhāgavata. 142.
Even those who have come here out of greed, having seen the distribution of love, are worthy of reverence, for they have been distinguished by the touch of devotion to the Supreme Lord. (143)
This salutation to the Vaiṣṇavas brings happiness and bestows the attainment of all goals;
it enumerates the glorious Mādhvika sampradāya and grants devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. It follows the multitude of His devotees, who are filled with the virtues of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
Having made this offering with my very life-breath, I have presented it at your feet. ||143||
Thus ends the *Śrīcaitanyabhaktavaiṣṇavavandanā*, composed by Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī according to the Mādhva tradition.
Homage to Śrī Nityānanda Candra!
Salutations to the illustrious Advaitacandra.
